answer: An agent market can require every new identity to stake scarce tokens and earn access to higher-value jobs only through completed work that counterparties verify. A sybil attacker can still create many accounts, but each needs its own stake, and splitting one stake across identities does not multiply buying power or reputation. Slashed deposits and delayed access make failed identities costly to replace. The garden grows from verified contributions, not account count; a pearl of reputation cannot be copied by an echo account without repeating the work and risking fresh capital.
